Q2_MChoice2: How is he?

Texto_lectura: We are at the supermarket. The name of this supermarket is "The big S". The watermelons and oranges are on sale. The carrots are in front of the tomatoes. I check the regular price of the milk and the bread. It is a good day to shop.
Q1_MChoice1: Which fruits are on sale?
Q2_MChoice2: Where are the carrots?

Texto_lectura: Hi! Let me tell you about my friend Alex. My friend is from Germany, but now he lives in China. His favorite foods are American meat and Guatemalan apples. He eats them every Sunday. His favorite number is 100. He is a very kind person. How old is he? He is 30 years old. We are good friends, and we like to study English together when we connect on Teams or WhatsApp.

Q2_MChoice2: What is his favorite food?
TF1: The friend lives in China.

Texto_lectura: Let me give you a tour of my favorite store This is 'The Global Bakery'. The bread here is very good. The owner is Mr. Cook; he is from Greece, but the coffee is from Brazil. On Thursdays, the Japanese rice cookies are on sale, and on Fridays you can buy Italian paninis! Today is Tuesday, and the bakery is very busy. People love to buy French products like the baguettes. They are delicious! I need 11 croissants for a meeting. The price is fourteen dollars ($14). I have a coupon: $14 minus $3.50 is $10.50. They always give coupons to the regular customers. Now you see why this is my favorite bakery!
Q1_MChoice1: Where is the coffee from?
Q2_MChoice2: 2. How much does the speaker pay after using the coupon?
TF1: On Tuesdays Italian products are on sale.
TF2_Question: You can buy Chinese cookies on Thursdays
TF3_Question: Today is Tuesday, and the bakery is very busy.

Texto_lectura: I am a young student. I am living in Canada, so every day I put some cream on my face because it is very cold outside. I drink a cup of hot coffee for a fast start to my day. This is a picture of me. I am the girl with curly hair that is smiling. I am thin, and a little tall. I am currently living in a new apartment with other students. I always try to be nice and polite with them. They say I'm creative and funny. This is an old building, but my bedroom is very comfortable.

A2_MChoice1: Because it is very cold outside.

Titulo_visible: The Real Routine of Cristiano Ronaldo
Texto_lectura:
What does Cristiano Ronaldo do away from the football cameras? His routine includes exercise, good food and family time.

In the morning, he <mark class="extra">drinks water</mark>, takes a short cold bath and <mark class="extra">takes a shower</mark>. He enjoys some morning sunlight before his coffee. To stay fit, he <mark class="extra">runs</mark> on the pitch and <mark class="extra">lifts weights</mark> in the gym. 

He <mark class="extra">eats</mark> fish, chicken, fruit and vegetables, and tries to avoid sugary foods. Cristiano also <mark class="extra">takes care of his body</mark> through rest. He checks his sleep with a small device on his wrist. His routine is not only about hard training.

In his free time, he <mark class="extra">spends time with his partner and children</mark>. Family time helps him relax. He also <mark class="extra">plays padel</mark> with close friends and likes to <mark class="extra">watch fights</mark>. Even a famous football player needs time for other interests and the people he loves.
Q1_MChoice1: How does Cristiano check his sleep?
A1_MChoice1: With a small device on his wrist.
A2_MChoice1: With a camera in his bedroom.
A3_MChoice1: With a notebook next to his bed.
Q2_MChoice2: Which sport does he play with close friends?
TF1: Cristiano drinks coffee before he enjoys the morning sunlight.
TF2_Question: He runs on the pitch and lifts weights in the gym.
TF3_Question: His routine includes time with his partner and children.
Vocabulary: drinks water (bebe agua):: takes water into the mouth and swallows it | takes a shower (se ducha):: washes the body under running water | runs (corre):: moves quickly on foot | lifts weights (levanta pesas):: raises heavy objects as exercise | eats (come):: takes food into the mouth | takes care of his body (cuida su cuerpo):: looks after his health and physical condition | spends time with his partner and children (pasa tiempo con su pareja e hijos):: does activities with his family | plays padel (juega pádel):: plays a racket sport on an enclosed court | watch fights (ver combates):: look at boxing or other combat sports

Titulo_visible: The Real Routine of Lester Martínez
Texto_lectura:
Lester Martínez is a professional boxer from Petén, Guatemala. His work takes him far from home, but Guatemala remains an important part of his life.

He <mark class="extra">trains</mark> in Guatemala and the United States. During training camps, he <mark class="extra">practices with other boxers</mark> and works closely with his coaches. These practice fights prepare him for the ring. Food experts help him <mark class="extra">eat well</mark>, keep his energy up and <mark class="extra">control his weight</mark>. Before a fight, he pays special attention to his food and water.

What does he miss away from home? Tortillas and Guatemalan food! He wants to enjoy these foods with <mark class="extra">family and friends</mark> when he returns. For Lester, going home means more than a break from boxing.

There is also a lighter side to his training. In one video on social media, he <mark class="extra">dances</mark> with Terence Crawford after a practice fight. They enjoy the song “Tu Sonrisa.” His training camp includes hard work, but also music and fun with a friend.
Q1_MChoice1: Who helps Lester with his food and weight?
Q2_MChoice2: What does Lester do with Terence Crawford in the video?
A3_MChoice2: He dances after a practice fight.
TF1: Lester trains only in Guatemala.
TF2_Question: He pays special attention to his food and water before a fight.
TF3_Question: He wants to enjoy Guatemalan food with family and friends.
Vocabulary: trains (entrena):: practices to improve physical or sporting skills | practices with other boxers (practica con otros boxeadores):: trains together with people who box | eat well (comer bien):: eat food that supports good health | control his weight (controlar su peso):: keep his body weight at a suitable level | family and friends (familia y amigos):: relatives and people someone likes and knows well | dances (baila):: moves the body to music

Texto_lectura:
A Big Problem: Tu Youyou is a scientist in China. She wants to help people. There is a terrible sickness called malaria. Many people get sick, and doctors need a new cure.

Looking for Answers: Tu Youyou does not give up. She reads very old books about traditional medicine and plants. She studies day and night, testing hundreds of different herbs to find a solution.
Finally, she <mark class="extra">discovers</mark> a special plant called "sweet wormwood". She <mark class="extra">discovers</mark> a clever way to get the medicine from the plant using cold liquids instead of hot ones, so the medicine does not break.

A Great Success: The new medicine is called "artemisinin". It works perfectly and cures the sickness. Tu Youyou saves millions of lives around the world and wins the Nobel Prize in Medicine.
Q1_MChoice1: Where does Tu Youyou look for answers?
A2_MChoice1: In old books about medicine and plants.
Q2_MChoice2: Why does she use cold liquids?
A1_MChoice2: To protect the medicine from damage.
A2_MChoice2: To make the plant grow faster.
A3_MChoice2: To change the color of the plant.
TF1: Tu Youyou tests only one herb.
TF2_Question: She gets the medicine from a plant called sweet wormwood.
TF3_Question: She wins the Nobel Prize in Medicine.
Vocabulary: discovers (descubre):: finds or learns something for the first time

Texto_lectura: Boyan Slat is a young Dutch inventor. When he was sixteen years old, he went diving in Greece and saw more plastic bags than fish in the sea. He felt deeply inspired to solve this global environmental problem. He was determined to make the oceans as clean as a whistle again. Boyan is an active and passionate leader. At the beginning, some people doubted his project. A few critics said he was just a fast talker who wanted easy attention. However, Boyan stayed confident. He designed advanced technology to trap plastic waste in rivers before it reaches the sea. His organization, The Ocean Cleanup, became one of the largest cleaning projects in history. Today, Boyan focuses on constructive solutions for our planet. His floating barriers are more productive than traditional boats with nets, and his team maintains a reliable system in the water. Thanks to his work, many rivers are now cleaner than before.
Q1_MChoice1: Why is collecting plastic in rivers important for Boyan’s goal?
A1_MChoice1: It stops some plastic from reaching the oceans.
A2_MChoice1: It moves plastic from the oceans into rivers.
A3_MChoice1: It makes more space for fishing boats.
Q2_MChoice2: What do Boyan’s actions show about him?
A1_MChoice2: He changes his goals whenever people criticize him.
A2_MChoice2: He prefers attention to finding useful solutions.
A3_MChoice2: He continues working even when others doubt him.
TF1: The expression “as clean as a whistle” describes how clean Boyan wants the oceans to be.
TF2_Question: The writer agrees with the critics who call Boyan a “fast talker.”
TF3_Question: Boyan’s project shows how a personal experience can lead to action on a global problem.

Texto_lectura: Katherine Johnson was an extraordinary African American mathematician who worked for NASA. From an early age, Katherine was an energetic and enthusiastic student. She loved numbers and was always the brightest pupil in her school. During the Space Race, NASA needed experts to calculate complex trajectories for astronauts. Katherine was a visionary thinker with a special talent for geometry. She was remarkably diligent with her calculations. In the 1960s, NASA began using sophisticated electronic machines, but the astronauts trusted Katherine more. Her work was more accurate than the early computers, and she showed the world that women were fully capable of leading scientific missions. Katherine felt deeply accountable for the lives of the astronauts. She was always committed to excellence and checked every equation several times. Even though she became one of the most important figures in space history, she was never big headed; she remained humble and always praised the power of teamwork.
Q1_MChoice1: Why did NASA need Katherine Johnson?
A1_MChoice1: To calculate complex trajectories for astronauts.
Q2_MChoice2: What made Katherine’s calculations special?
A1_MChoice2: They were more accurate than the early computers.
A2_MChoice2: They were faster than every modern computer.
TF1: Katherine loved numbers from an early age.
TF2_Question: The astronauts trusted the early electronic machines more than Katherine.
TF3_Question: Katherine remained humble and valued teamwork.

Texto_lectura: Last year, I found a job opening at a new bookstore in my town. It was a wonderful opportunity for me because I love reading. However, more than thirty people applied for the position, so I felt that getting the job would be a long shot. On the morning of the interview, my best friend texted me: "Break a leg!" That message made me smile and gave me confidence. At the store, I met the manager. I stayed calm and focused on every question. We talked about my professional goals for the future. I looked at the manager and said: "I can learn your cash register system fast, and I am a reliable worker who is always on time." At the end of our conversation, I smiled and said: "Thank you for your time. I look forward to hearing from you soon." The next day, the manager called me to say I got the job!
Q1_MChoice1: Where did the speaker apply for a job?
Q2_MChoice2: Who sent the speaker a message before the interview?
TF1: More than thirty people applied for the bookstore job.
TF2_Question: The speaker said they could learn the cash register system fast.
TF3_Question: The manager called the speaker one month after the interview.

Texto_lectura: Two years ago, I applied for a job as a receptionist at an international hotel. I studied interview questions every evening because I did not want my preparation to go down the drain. During the interview, the front desk manager asked about my previous work. I talked about my customer service experience in a small café. I also explained how my computer skills could help me register guests quickly. Before the meeting, I visited their website and read their mission statement. They wanted to make every traveler feel at home, and I expressed my sincere respect for that value. The manager told me that the schedule changes often. I told her that I am very flexible with morning and evening shifts. I also explained that I am a methodical person who likes to follow checklists and keep the reception desk clean and organized. She was very happy with my answers, and I started working there the following week.
Q1_MChoice1: What job did the speaker apply for?
Q2_MChoice2: Where did the speaker have customer service experience?
TF1: The speaker read the hotel’s mission statement on its website.
TF2_Question: The speaker could work only morning shifts.
TF3_Question: The speaker started working at the hotel the following week.

Texto_lectura: Last month, our neighborhood organized a big donation campaign for a local shelter. We wanted to help families in need, and the event was a great success. Here is what people donated and what we did: • First, we shared important information and news about the event on social media. • Many neighbors arrived and brought old luggage filled with winter clothes made of wool and cotton. • For the food bank, families collected a lot of produce, especially onions and carrots. • We didn't accept raw seafood or poultry products because we didn't have refrigerators at the park. • Instead, people gave non-perishable food and beverages, like bottled water, tea, and cold drinks. • A local store helped us and provided some dairy products. • Some volunteers built small boxes using wood and steel to organize all the donations. • At the end of the day, we felt a lot of love and happiness. We worked hard, but we had good luck with the weather!
Q1_MChoice1: Who did the neighborhood want to help?
Q2_MChoice2: Why did they not accept raw seafood or poultry?
A2_MChoice2: They did not have refrigerators at the park.
TF1: People shared information about the event on social media.
TF2_Question: The neighbors collected onions and carrots.
TF3_Question: The volunteers had bad luck with the weather.

Texto_lectura: Last month, I started an internship at a new office. On my first morning, our manager organized a group project. She explained that building good interpersonal connections is the first step to successful collaboration. At first, I felt nervous, but the team welcomed me warmly. After the first two days, our tasks were running smoothly, and I said to myself, "So far, so good." I wanted to be a helpful team player, so I practiced my communication skills by listening carefully to my coworkers. During our planning meetings, I spoke with calm assertiveness to share my opinions politely. This daily practice gave me more self-confidence. Our project required good time management because we had only three days to prepare the final presentation. When we had doubts about our project plan, we used critical thinking to analyze the situation. We also shared the decision-making process by voting on the best ideas. Working long hours was tiring, but my partner smiled and said, "No pain, no gain!" On Wednesday, a computer error deleted our presentation file. We were suddenly back to square one, but nobody panicked. We applied quick problem-solving methods and recreated the slides together. Thanks to our honest teamwork and strong work ethic, we finished the project before the deadline. At the end of the week, our supervisor gave us constructive feedback and praised our great rapport.
Q1_MChoice1: How did the team choose the best ideas?
A1_MChoice1: The intern chose all the ideas alone.
A2_MChoice1: They voted on the best ideas.
A3_MChoice1: They asked another company to choose.
Q2_MChoice2: What did the team do after the computer error?
A3_MChoice2: They waited for a new supervisor.
TF1: The intern listened carefully to coworkers to practice communication skills.
TF2_Question: The team had three weeks to prepare the final presentation.
TF3_Question: The team finished the project before the deadline.

Texto_lectura: Organic food is food that is produced without using chemicals. People buy organic food because they think it is healthy. But is it healthy for the planet? Most people think that organic food is grown by small local farmers. But today, giant food companies like Coca Cola also grow organic food. Many of these big companies still use conventional farming methods that are very bad for the environment, even if the food they grow is more "healthy." Another problem is that a lot of organic food actually comes from faraway countries. Gases from the trucks and airplanes that we use to transport our groceries across continents and countries are a major cause of global warming. What can you do if you want to buy organic food, but you also want to help the environment? One solution is to support your local farmer and encourage him to grow organic food. You can also join a community agriculture program. Members help pay for seeds, fertilizer, water, equipment, etc., and in return, the farm provides a healthy supply of fresh food. So the answer is to buy organic, but also buy local!
Q1_MChoice1: Why do many people buy organic food?
A1_MChoice1: Because they think it is healthy.
Q2_MChoice2: What is one way to help the environment?
A1_MChoice2: Buy organic food from faraway countries.
TF1: Organic food always comes from small local farmers.
TF2_Question: Transporting food long distances can cause global warming.
TF3_Question: A community agriculture program can provide fresh food.
Vocabulary: organic (orgánico):: produced according to organic farming rules | farmer (agricultor):: a person who grows crops or raises animals | conventional farming (agricultura convencional):: farming that uses common modern methods | fertilizer (fertilizante):: a substance added to soil to help plants grow | global warming (calentamiento global):: the long-term rise in average temperatures on Earth

Titulo_visible: A Green Box: Is It Organic?
Texto_lectura: Emma is at the supermarket with her dad. She wants some cereal for breakfast. “Look! This box is green. It has a tree and the words “100% natural.” Is it organic?” she asks. “Let’s read the label,” says Dad. “A picture of a tree does not mean the food is organic.” They look at another box. It has a small circle with the words “USDA Organic.” “This is an official seal in the United States,” Dad explains. “Farmers and food companies must follow special rules to use it.” “Does it mean all the ingredients are organic?” asks Emma. “Not always. For cereal with this seal, at least 95% of the ingredients must be organic. Water and salt do not count.” Emma looks at the two boxes again. “So, a green box and a nice picture are not enough!” “That’s right. Read the words, too.” Before they buy the cereal, Emma checks one more thing: the price!
Q1_MChoice1: What does a green box with a tree prove?
Q2_MChoice2: How many ingredients must be organic for the USDA seal?
TF1: The words “100% natural” always mean “organic.”
TF2_Question: The USDA Organic seal is an official seal in the United States.
TF3_Question: Water and salt count as organic ingredients.
Vocabulary: label (etiqueta):: a piece of information on a product or its package | seal (sello):: an official symbol showing that a product meets rules | rules (reglas):: instructions about what people must or must not do | at least (al menos):: not less than a particular amount | enough (suficiente):: as much or as many as needed

Titulo_visible: How to Pack an Emergency Backpack
Texto_lectura:
An <mark class="extra">emergency backpack</mark> can help you stay safe during an earthquake, a storm, or another emergency.

First, find a strong backpack.

Next, put three bottles of water inside.

Then, add some food that does not need a refrigerator, such as crackers or canned food.

After that, pack a <mark class="extra">flashlight</mark> and extra <mark class="extra">batteries</mark>.

Next, add a <mark class="extra">first-aid kit</mark> with bandages and basic medicine.

Then, put important <mark class="extra">documents</mark> in a <mark class="extra">waterproof</mark> bag.

After that, add a cell phone charger, a <mark class="extra">whistle</mark>, and a change of clothes.

Finally, keep the backpack in an easy-to-find place and <mark class="extra">check</mark> it every six months.
Q1_MChoice1: What should you pack first?
Q2_MChoice2: What type of food should you add?
A2_MChoice2: Food that does not need a refrigerator.
TF1: Extra batteries can help keep the flashlight working.
TF2_Question: Important documents should go in a waterproof bag.
TF3_Question: You should check the backpack every month.
Vocabulary: emergency backpack (mochila de emergencia):: a backpack with supplies for an emergency | flashlight (linterna):: a small portable light | batteries (baterías):: small objects that give power to devices | first-aid kit (botiquín de primeros auxilios):: a box or bag with basic medical supplies | whistle (silbato):: a small object that makes a loud sound | waterproof (impermeable):: able to keep water out | document (documento):: an official or important paper | check (revisar):: to look at something to make sure it is ready

Titulo_visible: How to Stay Safe During an Earthquake
Texto_lectura:
Earthquakes can happen without <mark class="extra">warning</mark>. It is important to know what to do before, during, and after an <mark class="extra">earthquake</mark>.

First, stay calm. Do not run or panic.

Next, get under a <mark class="extra">strong</mark> table or desk. If there is no table, sit next to an inside wall and protect your head and neck with your arms.

Then, stay away from windows, mirrors, and tall furniture. These objects can break or fall.

After that, wait until the shaking stops. Do not use elevators during an <mark class="extra">earthquake</mark>.

Next, check yourself and other people for <mark class="extra">injuries</mark>. Help others if you can.

Then, listen to the radio or check official information on your phone for emergency updates.

After that, if the building is <mark class="extra">damaged</mark>, leave carefully and go to an open area away from buildings, trees, and <mark class="extra">power lines</mark>.

Finally, stay with your family or friends and follow the instructions of emergency workers.
Q1_MChoice1: What should you do first during an earthquake?
Q2_MChoice2: What parts of your body should you protect?
TF1: Windows can break or fall during an earthquake.
TF2_Question: You can leave a damaged building carefully after the shaking stops.
TF3_Question: After leaving a damaged building, you should go to an open area away from buildings, trees, and power lines.
Vocabulary: earthquake (terremoto):: a sudden movement of the ground | warning (advertencia):: a message about possible danger | strong (resistente):: able to support weight without breaking | injury (lesión):: damage to a person's body | damaged (dañado):: harmed or broken | power line (línea eléctrica):: a cable that carries electricity

Texto_lectura: Paula Nicho Cumez is a Maya Kaqchikel artist from San Juan Comalapa. She is famous for her colorful paintings about Maya culture, nature, and community life. Paula usually gets up early in the morning. She always has breakfast before she starts working. After breakfast, she goes to her studio and begins painting. She often paints scenes from Maya traditions, nature, and daily life. She sometimes listens to music while she works. She often spends many hours painting and developing new ideas. At lunchtime, she takes a break and has lunch with her family. In the afternoon, she continues working on her paintings. She sometimes meets other artists and talks about art projects. Paula rarely travels for long periods because she enjoys spending time in her community, but she may travel for exhibitions and cultural events. She often observes nature and local traditions to find inspiration for her artwork. In the evening, she spends time with her family and reviews her sketches. She sometimes plans new paintings for the next day. She never stops learning about her culture and sharing it through her art. At night, she goes to bed and prepares for another creative day.
Q1_MChoice1: Which activity does Paula always do?
A1_MChoice1: She has breakfast before she starts working.
Q2_MChoice2: What does Paula often paint?
A2_MChoice2: Scenes from Maya traditions, nature, and daily life.
TF1: Paula sometimes listens to music while she paints.
TF2_Question: Paula rarely travels for long periods.
TF3_Question: Paula never stops learning about her culture and sharing it through her art.
Vocabulary: usually (normalmente):: on most occasions | always (siempre):: every time or on every occasion | often (a menudo):: many times | sometimes (a veces):: on some occasions | rarely (rara vez):: not often | never (nunca):: at no time | take a break (tomar un descanso):: stop an activity for a short rest

Texto_lectura: In this painting, by the famous artist Rosa Elena Curruchich, there is a baby who is ten days old. The family is celebrating an important moment. In the past, reaching ten days of life was a reason for great joy because many babies did not survive their first days. There is a large clay pot with hot water and medicinal herbs. The steam fills the room with pleasant aromas. There is a mother with her baby, and there is a group of women wearing colorful traditional huipiles. The women are helping and accompanying the family during the celebration. There are musicians playing traditional music. There are men playing the chirimía and the drum. Their music creates a ceremonial atmosphere. There are family members and neighbors sharing this special occasion together. There is a feeling of gratitude and happiness in the house. There are many traditions that make this celebration important. The painting shows community life, family support, and the protection of a newborn child.
Q1_MChoice1: How old is the baby?
Q2_MChoice2: What instruments are the men playing?
TF1: There is a large clay pot in the house.
TF2_Question: There are musicians at the celebration.
TF3_Question: The people feel gratitude and happiness during the celebration.
Vocabulary: newborn child (recién nacido):: a baby that was born very recently | steam (vapor):: hot water in the form of gas | clay pot (olla de barro):: a container made of baked clay

Texto_lectura:
Marjane Satrapi grew up in Iran during a time of major <mark class="extra">political change</mark>. When she was a child, new laws affected many people's daily lives. Marjane wanted to understand what was happening in her country and often asked questions about politics and society.

As a student, Marjane had the <mark class="extra">right</mark> to receive an education. She could learn about different subjects and discuss ideas with her family. However, life was not always easy. After the Revolution, girls had to wear a <mark class="extra">veil</mark> at school. Students had to follow new school rules, even if they did not always agree with them.

Marjane's parents believed that children should think <mark class="extra">independently</mark>. At home, she could express her opinions and ask difficult questions. She may not have understood every political event, but she was encouraged to learn and think critically.

Marjane also had responsibilities. She had to study, respect her teachers, and follow school <mark class="extra">policies</mark>. Her parents had to protect her and help her understand the changes taking place in Iran.

As she grew older, Marjane learned that people can have rights and responsibilities at the same time. <mark class="extra">Citizens</mark> can express their beliefs, but they also have to respect others. Her experiences taught her that understanding history and society is an important responsibility for everyone.
Q1_MChoice1: Where did Marjane Satrapi grow up?
Q2_MChoice2: What right did Marjane have as a student?
A1_MChoice2: The right to ignore school rules.
A2_MChoice2: The right to receive an education.
A3_MChoice2: The right to make new laws.
TF1: After the Revolution, girls had to wear a veil at school.
TF2_Question: At home, Marjane could express her opinions and ask difficult questions.
TF3_Question: Marjane had to study, respect her teachers, and follow school policies, while her parents had to protect her and help her understand the changes in Iran.
Vocabulary: political change (cambio político):: a major change in a government or political system | right (derecho):: something a person is allowed to have or do | veil (velo):: a piece of cloth worn to cover the hair or face | independently (de forma independiente):: without being controlled or helped by others | policy (norma):: an official rule or plan | citizen (ciudadano):: a person who legally belongs to a country

Texto_lectura: Which Island Destination Is Better? Many people dream about visiting tropical islands. Two popular destinations are Hawaii and Puerto Rico. Both places have beautiful beaches, warm weather, and interesting cultures, but they are different in several ways. Hawaii is larger than Puerto Rico and has more famous volcanoes. It is also farther from Guatemala. Puerto Rico is closer to Guatemala, so flights are often shorter. Puerto Rico is generally more Spanish-speaking than Hawaii. For many Guatemalans, Puerto Rico may feel more familiar because Spanish is the main language. In contrast, English is more common in Hawaii. When it comes to nature, Hawaii has some of the most spectacular landscapes in the world. Its volcanoes are more impressive than those of many other destinations. Puerto Rico, however, has one of the most beautiful rainforests in the Caribbean, El Yunque. Both destinations have excellent beaches. Some travelers think Hawaii has the best surfing beaches, while others prefer Puerto Rico because it is less expensive than Hawaii. In general, Hawaii is one of the most expensive vacation destinations in the United States. Food is another interesting difference. Puerto Rican food is spicier than Hawaiian food in some cases, while Hawaiian cuisine is more influenced by Asian cultures. In the end, neither destination is clearly better than the other. Hawaii may be the most exciting choice for travelers who love volcanoes and surfing. Puerto Rico may be the most convenient option for people who want a Caribbean experience in a Spanish-speaking environment.
Q1_MChoice1: What do both destinations have?
Q2_MChoice2: Which destination is closer to Guatemala?

Titulo_visible: Digital Credit Cards vs. Physical Credit Cards
Texto_lectura: Many people use credit cards to pay for products and services. Today, customers can choose between digital credit cards and physical credit cards. Both options are convenient, but they have important differences. A digital credit card is stored on a smartphone or smartwatch. A physical credit card is a plastic card that people carry in their wallets. Digital credit cards are generally more convenient than physical credit cards because people usually carry their phones everywhere. They are also faster than physical cards in many stores because customers can simply tap their devices. On the other hand, physical credit cards are more widely accepted than digital cards in some places. Not every business accepts digital payments. Physical cards are also easier to use than digital cards for people who are not comfortable with technology. In terms of security, many experts believe that digital credit cards are safer than physical cards because they often use biometric verification such as fingerprints or facial recognition. If a wallet is stolen, a thief may use a physical card more easily. However, if a phone is lost, users can often lock it remotely. Digital cards are also more environmentally friendly than physical cards because they do not require plastic. Physical cards, however, may be the most practical option when a phone battery is dead. For frequent travelers, digital wallets are often the most convenient payment method because they allow people to carry several cards on one device. However, many consumers still believe that physical cards are the most reliable option in emergencies. In conclusion, neither option is perfect. Digital credit cards are generally faster, safer, and more convenient, while physical credit cards are often more practical and more widely accepted. The best choice depends on the user's needs.
Q1_MChoice1: Where is a digital credit card stored?
Q2_MChoice2: Why do many experts consider digital credit cards safer?
A3_MChoice2: They are accepted by every business.
TF1: Digital credit cards are more widely accepted than physical cards in every place.
TF2_Question: Digital credit cards can be more environmentally friendly because they do not require plastic.
TF3_Question: A physical card may be the most practical option when a phone battery is dead.
Vocabulary: digital credit card (tarjeta de crédito digital):: a credit card stored on a smartphone or smartwatch | physical credit card (tarjeta de crédito física):: a plastic credit card carried in a wallet | widely accepted (ampliamente aceptado):: accepted in many places | biometric verification (verificación biométrica):: identity checking through fingerprints, facial recognition, or other body features | remotely (a distancia):: from another place using technology | environmentally friendly (ecológico):: causing less harm to the environment | practical (práctico):: useful and suitable for a situation | reliable (confiable):: able to work well when needed

Titulo_visible: Backstreet Boys vs. NSYNC: Which Boy Band Was More Successful?
Texto_lectura: In the late 1990s and early 2000s, Backstreet Boys and NSYNC were two of the biggest boy bands in the world. Backstreet Boys sold more than 100 million records worldwide. NSYNC sold about 70 million records worldwide. Therefore, Backstreet Boys were more successful than NSYNC in total record sales. However, NSYNC released one of the fastest-selling albums in music history. Their album No Strings Attached sold about 2.4 million copies in its first week in the United States. That was more than any other album at the time. Backstreet Boys had more international success than NSYNC. Their music was popular in Europe, Asia, and Latin America. They also completed larger world tours and performed in more countries. When it comes to awards, both groups were very successful. Backstreet Boys received more than 200 awards, while NSYNC won over 150 awards. Backstreet Boys were more recognized internationally, but NSYNC was often more popular among teenagers in the United States. Another important difference is the members' careers after the groups slowed down. Justin Timberlake became the most successful solo artist from either band. He won multiple Grammy Awards and sold millions of albums as a solo singer. Today, Backstreet Boys are still performing together more than 30 years after they were formed. They are one of the longest-lasting boy bands in pop music history. Many fans think they have the strongest vocal harmonies, while others believe NSYNC had the most exciting dance performances. In the end, Backstreet Boys were more successful in total sales, but NSYNC had one of the biggest albums ever released. Both groups remain among the most famous boy bands of all time. Statistics Backstreet Boys: 100+ million records sold NSYNC: 70+ million records sold No Strings Attached (NSYNC): 2.4 million copies sold in one week Backstreet Boys: 200+ awards NSYNC: 150+ awards Justin Timberlake: the most successful solo artist from either group
Q1_MChoice1: Which group sold more records worldwide?
A3_MChoice1: Both groups sold the same number.
Q2_MChoice2: How many records did Backstreet Boys sell worldwide?
TF1: NSYNC's No Strings Attached sold about 2.4 million copies in its first week.
TF2_Question: Backstreet Boys had more international success than NSYNC.
TF3_Question: Justin Timberlake became the most successful solo artist from either group.
Vocabulary: record sales (ventas de discos):: the number of music records or albums sold | worldwide (en todo el mundo):: in all parts of the world | fastest-selling album (álbum vendido más rápidamente):: an album that sells the most copies in a short time | copies (copias):: individual examples of an album, book, or other product | world tour (gira mundial):: a series of performances in different countries | recognized (reconocido):: known and respected by many people | solo artist (artista solista):: a performer who works independently rather than as part of a group | vocal harmonies (armonías vocales):: different sung notes that sound pleasant together

Titulo_visible: Australia vs. Canada: Job Opportunities Abroad
Texto_lectura: Many Latin Americans consider Australia and Canada when looking for better job opportunities abroad. Canada is often more popular because it has immigration programs for skilled workers and a large multicultural population. Nearly 23% of Canada's population consists of immigrants, so newcomers can meet people from many different cultures. On the other hand, Australia usually offers higher salaries in some industries, especially construction, mining, and engineering. About 31% of Australia's population was born overseas, which is a higher proportion than Canada's. This also makes Australia a very multicultural country. Canada is generally colder than Australia, but many people think it is easier to settle there because of its immigrant-friendly policies. For many newcomers, Canada is one of the most accessible countries for starting a new life. Australia is warmer than Canada and has a relaxed outdoor lifestyle that attracts many immigrants. However, it is farther from Latin America, so visiting family can be more difficult and expensive. Canada has larger Latin American communities, while Australia has some of the highest wages in the world. Both countries are safer than many Latin American countries and offer a high quality of life. Choosing between them depends on personal priorities. If someone wants the easiest immigration process, Canada may be the best option. If someone prefers a warmer climate and potentially higher earnings, Australia could be the better choice.
Q1_MChoice1: Why is Canada often popular with skilled workers?
A1_MChoice1: It has immigration programs and a multicultural population.
A3_MChoice1: It is closer to every Latin American country.
Q2_MChoice2: In which industries can Australia offer higher salaries?
TF1: Canada is generally colder than Australia.
TF2_Question: About 31% of Australia's population was born overseas.
TF3_Question: Australia is closer to Latin America than Canada.

Texto_lectura: Three astronauts travel to space on Apollo 13. Two days into the trip, an oxygen tank explodes. It is a serious emergency. The spacecraft loses electricity, water, and air. The astronauts are far away from Earth and are in great danger. In Houston, Texas, flight director Gene Kranz calls his entire team to Mission Control. He needs to rally the troops. The engineers are worried and scared, but Gene stays calm. He explains the situation clearly. He tells them, “Do not panic, and do not guess. Look at what still works and find solutions. Our only job is to bring our team home.” The team works together immediately: - One group calculates a new flight path around the Moon. - Another group finds ways to save battery power and water. - In a special room, engineers use simple items like tape, plastic bags, and socks to build an air filter for the astronauts. Everyone works day and night without stopping. After four days, the three astronauts land safely in the Pacific Ocean. Gene Kranz rallies the troops, and great teamwork saves three lives. This story is portrayed in the movie Apollo 13, starring Tom Hanks.

A2_MChoice1: The astronauts land on the Moon.
Q2_MChoice2: What do the engineers use to build an air filter?

TF2_Question: Gene Kranz tells the team not to panic or guess.
TF3_Question: After four days, the astronauts land safely in the Pacific Ocean.

Simone inspires athletes around the world. She teaches people that hard work and courage can help them achieve great things. Because of her success, gymnastics is different today. Texto_lectura: Every day is busy at Bright Ideas Company. Daniel is a Sales Representative. He goes to work at 8:00 a.m. and starts work at 8:30. In the morning, he makes phone calls and talks to customers. He also makes appointments with new clients. He keeps a yellow notebook on his desk and writes down each customer's name before a call. Daniel believes good communication helps the company achieve its goals. Sofia is a Marketing Specialist. She usually starts work at 8:30 a.m., but on Mondays she arrives at 7:00 to prepare a special meeting. Every Monday, she attends a meeting with the marketing team. She prepares reports about marketing campaigns and focuses on new ideas. Her team advertises the company's products on social media and promotes special offers. Sofia anticipates customers' needs to help boost sales. Carlos is a Project Manager. He usually attends meetings with different departments and gives presentations about new projects. He also talks to customers and checks his team's results. Carlos believes everybody benefits from good teamwork. His team works hard to achieve its objectives. When they have new projects, they sometimes finish work at 7:00 p.m. On these evenings, Carlos always orders dinner for them and pays them for the extra hours. They share pizza around the meeting table before going home. He thanks his team for keeping their eyes on the prize: finishing the project well.

Texto_lectura: Loroco is a special flower used in Central American food. In Guatemala, many people use loroco to prepare delicious dishes. It has a strong smell and a special flavor. One popular dish is chicken with loroco. To prepare it, we need some chicken, some loroco, an onion, and a few tomatoes. We also need a little salt and some cream. We don't need much oil, but we need a lot of flavor! Loroco is also excellent with cheese. Some people make pupusas with cheese and loroco, and others add it to soups, rice, or sauces. Are there many ingredients in these dishes? Sometimes! But you don't need any difficult ingredients to enjoy loroco. With a few vegetables, some cheese, and a little loroco, you can prepare something delicious. For many families, loroco is more than an ingredient. It is part of traditional food and a flavor that makes a meal special.
Q1_MChoice1: What is loroco?
A2_MChoice1: A special flower used in Central American food
Q2_MChoice2: What ingredients do you need for chicken with loroco?
A1_MChoice2: Chicken, loroco, onion, tomatoes, salt, and cream
A2_MChoice2: Beef, potatoes, carrots, and a lot of oil
TF1: Loroco has a strong smell and a special flavor.
TF2_Question: You need a lot of oil to prepare chicken with loroco.
TF3_Question: Some people make pupusas with cheese and loroco.
Vocabulary: loroco (loroco):: an edible flower used in Central American cooking | flavor (sabor):: the taste of food or drink | onion (cebolla):: a round vegetable with layers and a strong smell | tomatoes (tomates):: soft red fruits commonly used as vegetables | salt (sal):: a substance used to season food | cheese (queso):: a food made from milk | soups (sopas):: liquid foods made with vegetables or other ingredients | sauces (salsas):: liquids added to food for flavor | ingredients (ingredientes):: foods used together to prepare a dish | traditional food (comida tradicional):: food associated with the customs of a place or community

Texto_lectura: In Guatemala, addresses are special. In Guatemala City, people use words like calle, avenida, and zona. A common address is 6a Avenida, Zona 1. A calle is a street and an avenida is an avenue. But when we speak English, we usually keep these names in Spanish. Outside the capital, addresses change. You can see words like municipio, aldea, cantón, and colonia. These words are not easy to translate. The United States uses words like city, town, village, drive, or lane. They are not the same thing. For this reason, do not translate your local address. Keep the original words so people can find your home. Learning English is not only about new words. It is also about learning how different people live and organize their communities. Every country has its own way of writing addresses.
Q1_MChoice1: Why should you keep your local address in Spanish?
A1_MChoice1: So people can easily find your home.
A2_MChoice1: Because English has no words for streets.
A3_MChoice1: Because the post office is always closed.
Q2_MChoice2: Which words are commonly used outside Guatemala City?
TF1: In Guatemala City, addresses often use calle, avenida, and zona.
TF2_Question: The text advises you to translate your home address into English.
TF3_Question: Learning English also includes understanding how communities organize themselves.
Vocabulary: address (dirección):: the details of where a building or home is located | street (calle):: a road in a city or town with houses or buildings | avenue (avenida):: a broad street or road | translate (traducir):: to change words from one language into another | community (comunidad):: a group of people living in the same area

Titulo_visible: The Man on the Green Cover
Texto_lectura:
Look at this man. His name is Al-Khwarizmi. He lived a long time ago. He is the father of algebra.

Today, his face is on old stamps. But in Latin America, his face is very famous for a different reason: the green cover of the Álgebra de Baldor!

Right now, students all over the world open their notebooks. They look at the green book. They read math problems. They write numbers, letters, and <mark class="extra">equations</mark>.

For example, they can write: 50 + 50 = 100. They say, “Fifty <mark class="extra">plus</mark> fifty <mark class="extra">equals</mark> one hundred.” They can also write: 100 - 25 = 75. They say, “One hundred <mark class="extra">minus</mark> twenty-five <mark class="extra">equals</mark> seventy-five.”

In algebra, students also use letters. For example: x + 20 = 100. What is x? The answer is 80! Eighty <mark class="extra">plus</mark> twenty <mark class="extra">equals</mark> one hundred.

Students also practice other math signs: + means <mark class="extra">plus</mark>, - means <mark class="extra">minus</mark>, × means <mark class="extra">times</mark>, ÷ means <mark class="extra">divided by</mark>, and = means <mark class="extra">equals</mark>.

Sometimes students say, “Oh no, more homework!” Al-Khwarizmi is quiet on the cover, but his math is in every school. Students practice numbers and <mark class="extra">equations</mark> every day!
Q1_MChoice1: Why is Al-Khwarizmi's face famous in Latin America?
A1_MChoice1: Because it appears on the cover of Álgebra de Baldor.
A2_MChoice1: Because he was an international soccer player.
A3_MChoice1: Because he lives in Guatemala today.
Q2_MChoice2: In the equation "x + 20 = 100", what is the value of x?
TF1: Al-Khwarizmi is known as the father of algebra.
TF2_Question: The math sign "+" means minus.
TF3_Question: In algebra, students practice both numbers and letters.
Vocabulary: Cover (portada o cubierta):: The outer front or back part of a book | Face (rostro o cara):: The front part of a person's head with the eyes, nose, and mouth | Look at (mirar u observar):: To direct your eyes toward someone or something | Famous (famoso o conocida):: Known by many people | Lived (vivió):: The past form of live, meaning had life or a home in a specific time or place | Appear (aparecer):: To be seen or show up in a particular place | Centuries ago (hace siglos):: Many hundreds of years in the past

My coworker is putting staplers and tape dispensers on the shelves. Another coworker is carrying clipboards around the office. The office also has many desks, filing cabinets, and waste baskets. Q2_MChoice2: What items is the speaker organizing right now?

Texto_lectura: Three years ago, I heard a noise in the back of my apartment. It was a cat that had fallen onto my roof. I tried to catch it, but it was very evasive. It was very difficult to get it out. (It took 3 or 4 days). Today, the cat's scratches are still on the furniture. Now, it's your turn. Texto_lectura: Ecosia is a special search engine and web browser. It is similar to Google, but it helps the planet. How does it work? When you use Ecosia to discover new things on the internet, you see ads. Different companies advertise their products on the results page. Ecosia uses the money from these ads to plant trees in many countries around the world. What is it used for? You use it to find information online. The creators of Ecosia believe that simple actions can change the world. They focus on planting trees in places where nature needs help. Many animals and local communities benefit from these new forests. If we use this browser every day, we can help achieve a greener and healthier planet!

Texto_lectura:
Plants are beautiful and very useful. Some plants look good in your house, and other plants are good for your health!

The <mark class="extra">Snake Plant</mark> (Sansevieria) is an excellent plant for <mark class="extra">beginners</mark>. It is very strong, and it cleans the air in your room. You don't need to water it often. You just need to give it water <mark class="extra">once a month</mark>. It likes <mark class="extra">sunlight</mark>, but it can live in dark places too. You should clean its long <mark class="extra">leaves</mark> <mark class="extra">twice a year</mark> to keep it healthy.

<mark class="extra">Basil</mark> is another wonderful plant. It is a delicious herb, and it smells great. You can use it to cook pasta or make pizza. <mark class="extra">Basil</mark> needs more attention than the <mark class="extra">Snake Plant</mark>. You must water your <mark class="extra">basil</mark> plant every day or <mark class="extra">three times a week</mark> if the weather is cold. It loves the sun, so it is perfect for a kitchen window.

Having plants is fun! They give life to your home. Do you have any plants?
Q1_MChoice1: Which plant is described as needing water once a month?
Q2_MChoice2: Where does the text suggest keeping basil?
TF1: The snake plant has long leaves.
TF2_Question: Basil needs less attention than the snake plant.
TF3_Question: Basil can be used to cook pasta or make pizza.

Texto_lectura:
Hello! My name is Carlos. Spanish is my native language. In Spanish, we have five vowel sounds, and we read the words exactly as we write them. But English is different. In English, there are 15 vowel sounds! This is very difficult for me because the letters and the sounds are not the same. I need to listen carefully and practice my pronunciation every day in class.
Here are some examples for you:
/ʌ/ (Short 'u'): This sound comes from the throat. It is very short and relaxed, like a quick Spanish "a".
Words: Cup, Bus, Sun, Run, Fun, Up.

/i:/ (Long 'e' / The smiling vowel): This is a long sound. You stretch your mouth into a smile when you say it.
Words: See, Meet, Tree.

/æ/ (Between 'a' and 'e'): To make this sound, open your mouth like you want to say "a", but try to say "e".
Words: Cat, Apple, Hat.

/ə/ (Schwa): This is the most common sound in English. It is a very short, quiet, and relaxed sound. You only hear it in syllables that do not have the stress or accent.
Words: About, Teacher, Listen.
Q1_MChoice1: How many vowel sounds are there in English according to the text?
Q2_MChoice2: What is the most common vowel sound in English?
TF1: Spanish has 15 vowel sounds.
TF2_Question: The sound /ʌ/ comes from the throat.
TF3_Question: You only hear the schwa in syllables with no stress (acento)

Titulo_visible: The origin of All Saints' Day
Texto_lectura:
All Saints' Day is celebrated on November 1st. This celebration from the Celts, a group of people who lived in Europe many years ago. The Celts had a festival in early November because they believed that spirits visit the living on this date. Many years later, the Catholic Church chose November 1st to remember the saints and the people who are no longer in the world.

Today, many countries use this date to celebrate and remember their family members:
Mexico: They celebrate the "Day of the Dead". Families put orange flowers and photos in their houses.
Spain: People go to the cemetery and eat small traditional sweets.
Philippines: Families light candles and have a big picnic in the cemetery to be close to the spirits.
Q1_MChoice1: When did the Celts celebrate their festival?
Q2_MChoice2: What do families do in Mexico on Day of the Dead?
A2_MChoice2: They put orange flowers and photos in their houses.
A3_MChoice2: They light candles for a picnic in the park.
TF1: All Saints Day is celebrated on November 1st.
TF2_Question: In Spain, people eat small traditional sweets at the cemetery.
TF3_Question: In the Philippines, families stay away from the cemetery.
